note: The measures the three hybrids are judged on. WRITTEN BEFORE ANY HYBRID WAS RUN, and not edited afterwards. A measure invented after seeing a leaderboard measures the person who invented it. The regexes below were written from the query strings alone.
universe: plotted (1541 films). The fact check asks whether a retrieved film's text contains the thing the query named; on a 200-char description tier an absence is a gap in the TEXT, not in the film, so the fact measure runs only where a full plot exists. Every other measure runs on all 2204.

biasDeclaration.FACT: DENSE-FAVOURING, twice. (a) it scores presence in exactly the text the dense index embedded, and (b) the incumbent never saw plot text at all and can only hit these through attribute correlation. A dense win here is close to tautological and is reported as such. An INCUMBENT or HYBRID win here is the informative outcome.
biasDeclaration.NEGVIOL: ATLAS-FAVOURING. It is scored off the same 59-attribute table match.js scores from. It is kept because it is a correctness measure, not a preference: a ranker that puts graphically violent films at the top of 'a revenge film that isn't violent' is wrong in a way no taste argument rescues.
biasDeclaration.WATCH: NEUTRAL, and the only pre-registered relevance labels in the repo. Taken verbatim from bakeoff-battery.json and bakeoff-queries.json, both frozen before this stage existed.
biasDeclaration.FAME: NEUTRAL. AGENTS rule 1. Reported for every method including the pure sides.

fact.note: A film counts as a hit if its plot text matches the regex, case-insensitive. Queries are included ONLY where the query names a thing that literally happens on screen and would leave a lexical trace in a plot summary. Mood, shape and tone queries are deliberately EXCLUDED: a felt quality has no literal term, and a regex there would measure vocabulary overlap rather than relevance, which is the very confusion this bake-off exists to settle.
fact.q22: deaf|hearing loss|losing (his|her|their) hearing|going deaf|tinnitus|hard of hearing

excluded.q13: carries a negation ('but not about the fighting') — the literal war terms would reward exactly the films the query excludes
excluded.q12: 'set almost entirely in one room' leaves no reliable lexical trace
excluded.q04-q11,q16-q19,q27-q29: mood / shape / tone / quiet — no literal term by construction

negation.note: The parser reports which attribute it negated. A top-10 slot VIOLATES if the film carries that attribute in the same consensus table match.js scores from. Lower is better; 0 is clean.

q26.caveat: the parser reads 'love' as subject:desire POSITIVELY and 'not romantic' as the same attribute NEGATED, so the query self-cancels inside the vocabulary. Reported, not scored as a clean negation.

watch.note: Pre-registered relevance labels, copied verbatim from the frozen query files. Rank of each film under each method.

expect.old joy: SHOULD RANK HIGH on q02 — the friendship that quietly ends. Fingerprint distance buried it at #1291/2197.
expect.close: SHOULD RANK HIGH on q02 — a friendship that ruptures.
expect.ex machina: SHOULD RANK LOW on q02 — the cold ironic two-hander fingerprint distance wrongly promoted to 2.8 of ~200.
expect.the banshees of inisherin: ambiguous — it IS the reference film for the query, so a high rank is neither a win nor a loss.
expect.the conversation: SHOULD RANK HIGH on q01 — the surveillance film.

fame.proxy: imdbVotes from rag-audit-facts.json, log10, Spearman against rank. The dense side's own rating source, so no new fame number is invented here.
fame.direction: POSITIVE rho = the method prefers famous films = the thing AGENTS rule 1 forbids. Negative is fine.

other: TIE WIDTH at rank 1 — how many films share the top score. match.js breaks ties alphabetically, so a wide band is a band, not an identification.
REACH — distinct films appearing in any top-10 across all 30 queries, out of a 300 ceiling. A method that returns the same canon every time has low reach.
SHIPPABILITY — can this run at build time and ship as data in one HTML file with no runtime model.
